 Social Security COLA 2027: When Higher Payments Start in Florida, Texas and California
 By: Daniel Brooks 
 | 
 Editor: Matthew Reed 
 November 17, 2026, 02:29 WITA · 5 min read 
 Illustration of Social Security benefits and U.S. currency ahead of the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), which will increase monthly payments for eligible Americans. 
 BALTIMORE, Aktualita.co -  Millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits will see larger monthly payments in 2027 following a confirmed 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), providing additional income to retirees, people with disabilities and other eligible beneficiaries. 
 The increase will take effect with Social Security benefits paid in January 2027, while recipients of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) will receive their adjusted January benefits earlier, on December 31, 2026. 
 Advertisement 
 For beneficiaries in Florida, Texas and California, the payment dates will follow the same federal schedule used nationwide. The amount of the increase, however, will depend on each recipient's existing benefit. 
 The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced the adjustment on October 14, 2026, confirming that approximately 76 million Americans will be affected. 
 According to the agency, the average retired worker will receive approximately $75 more per month, bringing estimated average monthly retirement benefits to $2,170. 
 When Will Social Security COLA 2027 Payments Begin? 
 The 3.6% increase applies to Social Security benefits for December 2026, which are generally paid during January 2027. 
 Most beneficiaries receive payments according to their birth dates. Under the SSA's official 2027 payment calendar, the January distribution dates are: 
 January 13, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th of the month. 
 January 20, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th. 
 January 27, 2027: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st. 
 Different payment rules apply to people who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 and those who receive both Social Security and SSI. 
 These beneficiaries generally follow the third-of-the-month payment schedule, with adjustments when the scheduled date falls on a weekend or federal holiday. 
 Recipients should check their individual payment notices to confirm their expected deposit dates. 
 Florida, Texas and California: Will Payment Dates Be Different? 
 Social Security is administered federally, meaning residents of Florida, Texas and California receive the same percentage increase and generally follow the same national payment schedule. 
 In Florida, retirees living in Miami, Orlando, Tampa and other communities will receive their adjusted benefits according to their assigned federal payment dates. 
 The same rules apply in Texas, including Houston, Dallas, Austin and San Antonio. 
 California residents in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Sacramento and San Diego will also follow the nationwide schedule. 
 There is no separate Social Security COLA percentage for any of these states. 
 However, some SSI recipients may qualify for additional state-funded assistance, particularly in California, where the state operates a supplementary payment program. 
 Such supplements are separate from the federal COLA, and total SSI payments may differ depending on individual eligibility and living arrangements. 
 How Much Will Social Security Payments Increase in 2027? 
 The SSA's official 2027 COLA fact sheet provides estimated monthly benefit amounts for several recipient categories. 
 For retired workers, the average monthly benefit is expected to rise from $2,095 to approximately $2,170. 
 Couples in which both spouses receive retirement benefits are projected to receive an average combined payment of $3,355, compared with $3,238 before the adjustment. 
 For disabled workers, the estimated average monthly benefit will increase from $1,642 to $1,701. 
 The federal SSI maximum payment will also rise. An eligible individual can receive up to $1,029 per month in 2027, compared with $994 in 2026. 
 For an eligible couple, the maximum federal SSI payment increases from $1,491 to $1,544. 
 These figures represent federal estimates or maximums, not guaranteed payments for every beneficiary. 
 Actual benefit amounts vary according to earnings history, retirement age, eligibility and applicable deductions. 
 SSI Recipients Will Receive Their Increase in December 2026 
 Unlike regular Social Security retirement benefits, the first increased SSI payment for 2027 is scheduled for December 31, 2026. 
 That payment represents January 2027 benefits, arriving early because January 1 is a federal holiday. 
 Recipients should not interpret the December payment as an additional bonus or separate benefit. 
 The SSA estimates that approximately 7.3 million people receiving SSI will benefit from the adjustment. 
 Some Americans receive both SSI and regular Social Security benefits, meaning their two payments may follow different schedules. 
 SSA Commissioner Confirms the 2027 Benefit Increase 
 In its October 14 announcement, the Social Security Administration emphasized the financial importance of the annual adjustment. 
 “Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” said Frank J. Bisignano, Commissioner of Social Security. 
 The COLA is calculated using changes in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, commonly known as CPI-W. 
 The index is maintained by the Bureau of Labor Statistics and measures changes in prices paid by certain urban households. 
 The annual adjustment is intended to help Social Security benefits keep pace with inflation, although individual household expenses may rise at different rates. 
 Could Medicare Premiums Reduce the Increase? 
 Although the 3.6% adjustment increases gross Social Security benefits, the amount deposited into a recipient's bank account may be affected by Medicare deductions. 
 Many beneficiaries have Medicare Part B premiums deducted directly from their Social Security payments. 
 Changes in those premiums can therefore reduce the net increase recipients actually receive. 
 For this reason, retirees should review both their updated gross benefit and any deductions before estimating their available monthly income for 2027. 
 How to Check Your New Social Security Benefit Amount 
 The SSA will make personalized COLA notices available through eligible beneficiaries' my Social Security accounts beginning in late November 2026. 
 Beneficiaries who want early online access must establish their accounts and enroll in paperless notices by November 18, 2026. 
 People who do not receive paperless notices will generally receive their updated benefit information by mail in December. 
 The personalized notice will explain the recipient's revised monthly benefit and any applicable deductions. 
 Beneficiaries do not need to submit a separate application to receive the annual COLA increase. 
 What Beneficiaries Should Know Before January 2027 
 For retirees and other beneficiaries across Florida, Texas and California, the most important change is already confirmed: Social Security payments will increase by 3.6% in 2027. 
 Most regular beneficiaries can expect the adjustment in January, while SSI recipients will see their first increased payment on December 31, 2026. 
 With the new payment dates approaching, recipients should review their SSA notices, verify their direct deposit information and account for possible Medicare deductions when planning their household budgets.
